ukmt-jk-2025-01.title: Count the lines of symmetry
ukmt-jk-2025-01.body:
The second and fourth signs have no line of symmetry, the first and fifth have one, and the third (a horizontal bar in a circle) has two: one horizontal and one vertical.

**Answer: (C)**

ukmt-jk-2025-02.title: Subtract the corners
ukmt-jk-2025-02.body: Four right triangles with legs 5 cm are cut off, each of area $12.5\text{ cm}^2$. The smaller square has area $100-50=50$.

ukmt-jk-2025-02.title: Halve the big square
ukmt-jk-2025-02.body:
The smaller square's diagonals are the sides of the big square's halves; the square joining the midpoints is exactly half the big square. $100\div2=50$.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-jk-2025-03.title: Count wrong items
ukmt-jk-2025-03.body:
Four items of cutlery are in the wrong place and each swap fixes at most two of them, so at least $4\div2=2$ swaps are needed. Two swaps suffice, e.g. swap the knife and fork on the third plate, and swap the misplaced fork on the first plate with the misplaced knife on the second plate.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-jk-2025-04.title: Pair by pair
ukmt-jk-2025-04.body:
Two girls facing each other lie on opposite sides, so exactly one has her right ear down. The same holds for two girls with their backs to each other. So $1+1=2$.

**Answer: (C)**

ukmt-jk-2025-05.title: Opposite faces
ukmt-jk-2025-05.body:
In the net, $P$ is opposite $S$ and $R$ is opposite $T$; no face is opposite $Q$. In an open box the base has no opposite face (the top is open), so the base is $Q$.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-jk-2025-06.title: Check each option
ukmt-jk-2025-06.body:
Figure A would need an equilateral triangle at the top, but the angle there is a corner of a square, $90^\circ$, so A is impossible. The others can all be formed by overlapping two squares at suitable positions or rotations.

**Answer: (A)**

ukmt-jk-2025-07.title: Factorise
ukmt-jk-2025-07.body:
$2025=45^2=(3^2\cdot5)^2=3^4\cdot5^2$, so the distinct primes are 3 and 5.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-jk-2025-08.title: Track the times
ukmt-jk-2025-08.body:
Measure time in units of one space. After one unit V, X, Y and Z have each reached their nearest nut, and are then 3, 3, 4 and 6 spaces from the next nearest nut. W is still 2 spaces from its nearest nut and gets there before V. The only remaining nut is the one X, Y and Z are all heading for, and X is closest, so X gets two nuts.

**Answer: (C)**

ukmt-jk-2025-09.title: Count by pairs
ukmt-jk-2025-09.body:
Each boy sits with a girl, so if there are $x$ boys there are $x$ girls sitting next to a boy. These are half of the girls, so there are $2x$ girls. Then $x+2x=30$ and $x=10$.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-jk-2025-10.title: Keep the pieces short
ukmt-jk-2025-10.body:
Ten digits split into three pieces means some piece has at least 4 digits. The best splits are 4+3+3 digits: $2581+953+764=4298$, $258+1953+764=2975$, $258+195+3764=4217$. Other splits (4+4+2 or longer pieces) give larger sums. The smallest is 2975.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-jk-2025-11.title: Cat-days
ukmt-jk-2025-11.body:
The food is $4\times12=48$ cat-days. With six cats it lasts $48\div6=8$ days.

**Answer: (A)**

ukmt-jk-2025-12.title: Digit sum
ukmt-jk-2025-12.body:
$N$ appears twice and every other letter once, so the digit sum is $28+N$. The number is odd, so $N$ is odd: $28+N\in\{29,31,33,35\}$ for $N=1,3,5,7$. Only 33 is divisible by 3, so $N=5$.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-jk-2025-13.title: Write the total
ukmt-jk-2025-13.body:
If the triplets are $x$ years old, the sum is $3x+(x-3)=4x-3$, which is 3 less than a multiple of 4. Adding 3 to the options gives $56,57,59,62,66$; only 56 is a multiple of 4. So the sum is 53 (triplets 14, Carl 11).

**Answer: (A)**

ukmt-jk-2025-14.title: Effect of one added rectangle
ukmt-jk-2025-14.body:
A rectangle of size $2x\times2y$ centred at a corner adds $(x+2y)+(2x+y)$ to the boundary and removes $x+y$, a net gain of $2x+2y$, which is half of its perimeter. For three rectangles the net gain is $\frac12\times20=10$ cm, so the new perimeter is $30+10=40$ cm.

**Answer: (C)**

ukmt-jk-2025-15.title: List them
ukmt-jk-2025-15.body:
The digits after the 1 sum to 4 and are non-decreasing (and at least 1): 11111, 1112, 113, 14, 122. That is 5 integers.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-jk-2025-16.title: Upper bound and construction
ukmt-jk-2025-16.body:
Each shape covers 4 squares and the grid has 25, so at most $\lfloor25/4\rfloor=6$ shapes fit. It is possible to cut out 6 shapes (leaving one square), so the answer is 6.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-jk-2025-17.title: Set up equations
ukmt-jk-2025-17.body: Let there be $2x$ tables. Chairs: $4\cdot2x-6=8x-6$, and also $6x+4$. So $8x-6=6x+4$, $x=5$ and there are 10 tables.

ukmt-jk-2025-17.title: Compare the two plans
ukmt-jk-2025-17.body:
Per pair of tables, plan 1 needs 8 chairs and plan 2 uses 6. The difference per pair is 2 chairs, and the total difference is $6+4=10$ chairs. So there are $10\div2=5$ pairs, i.e. 10 tables.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-jk-2025-18.title: Smallest enclosing triangle
ukmt-jk-2025-18.body:
The shape contains a line of five tiles with further tiles on each side, so the large triangle has a side with at least seven tiles. A triangle with 7 tiles along its longest row has $7+5+3+1=16$ tiles, and it can be built around the given shape (which has 7 tiles). So $16-7=9$ more tiles are needed.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-jk-2025-19.title: Translate a side
ukmt-jk-2025-19.body: $PQ$ and $SR$ are parallel and equal. From $P$ to $Q$ is $+6$ in $x$ and $+3$ in $y$, so $S=R-(6,3)=(-1,5)$.

ukmt-jk-2025-19.title: Use the centre
ukmt-jk-2025-19.body:
The diagonals bisect each other. The midpoint of $QS$ equals that of $PR$, which is $(3,4.5)$. So $S=2(3,4.5)-(7,4)=(-1,5)$.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-jk-2025-20.title: Count black squares
ukmt-jk-2025-20.body:
Each small cube shows three of its faces on three faces of the large cube, so the total number of black squares over the six faces is a multiple of three. The five faces shown have $2+1+1+1+1=6$, so the sixth face has 0 or 3 black squares, leaving options A and E. In E two black squares would share an edge, but no shown face has two such squares adjacent. So the sixth face is all white.

**Answer: (A)**

ukmt-jk-2025-21.title: Total area is double
ukmt-jk-2025-21.body:
Let the width be $Y$. The pool plus path is $24\times(Y+4)$ and equals twice the pool area: $24(Y+4)=40Y$, so $96=16Y$ and $Y=6$.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-jk-2025-22.title: Compare adjacent sides
ukmt-jk-2025-22.body:
Call $p$ the empty corner circle on the left, $q$ the empty corner circle at the bottom left and $r$ the empty corner circle at the bottom right. The side through $3$ and $7$ has corners $p$ and $7$, and the next side has $p,1,q$. Equal sums give $7+3+p=p+1+q$, so $q=9$. The side $q,6,r$ and the side $r,2,X$ give $q+6+r=r+2+X$, so $X=q+4=13$.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-jk-2025-23.title: Parity argument
ukmt-jk-2025-23.body:
Each calculation changes the exponent of 2 or of 3 in the result by exactly 1, so after 60 calculations the total change in the two exponents is even. Now $12=2^2\cdot3$ and $36=2^2\cdot3^2$ differ by 1 in total, which is odd, so 36 is impossible. The others differ from 12 by an even total: $18=2\cdot3^2$ (change $-1+1$), $72=2^3\cdot3^2$ ($+1+1$), $108=2^2\cdot3^3$ ($+2$), $12$ (change 0). Each can be reached by using some of the calculations in cancelling pairs such as $\times2$ then $\div2$.

**Answer: (C)**

ukmt-jk-2025-24.title: Translate to equations
ukmt-jk-2025-24.body:
$Y+Z=Y$ gives $Z=0$. Then $2X+Y=10Y$, so $2X=9Y$. Hence $2X$ is a multiple of 9, so $X=9$ and $Y=2$.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-jk-2025-25.title: Minimise the hundreds digits
ukmt-jk-2025-25.body:
The hundreds digits sum to at least 5: either $1$ and $4$ (last digit 2 in the first number) or $2$ and $3$ (with a last digit 1). In the first case the tens digits can be 0 and 3; in the second 0 and 4, so the first case is better. Example: $102+435=537$.

**Answer: (C)**
